name: TIME
fix_description: In MulticallUpgradeable.multicall, when the call originates from a trusted forwarder (isTrustedForwarder(msg.sender)), append the original _msgSender() (extracted from calldata tail per ERC2771) to each sub-call's data before delegatecall. This ensures _msgSender() in each sub-call resolves to the actual meta-transaction signer, not an attacker-controlled suffix. Without this, an attacker can craft multicall sub-call data with an arbitrary address appended at the end, and since delegatecall preserves the trusted forwarder as msg.sender, _msgSender() in the sub-call reads the attacker-spoofed address — enabling unauthorized burns or transfers on behalf of any victim.
difficulty_reasoning: The exploit is not a simple single-call bug: it requires understanding the ERC2771Context + Multicall arbitrary sender spoofing issue, crafting/using a valid forwarder request, and then leveraging the resulting unauthorized burn to manipulate a Uniswap pair before syncing and swapping for profit. The PoC is still fairly compact and only involves a few contracts and steps, so it is more involved than easy but not deep enough to be hard.
